executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

# go-mod-outdated

An easy way to find outdated dependencies of your Go projects.

go-mod-outdated provides a table view of the **go list -u -m -json all** command which lists all dependencies of a Go project and their available minor and patch updates. It also provides a way to filter indirect dependencies and dependencies without updates.

## What it does

go-mod-outdated takes JSON output from `go list` and converts it into an easy-to-read table format showing:
- Module name
- Current version
- Available new version (if any)
- Whether it's a direct or indirect dependency
- Whether the timestamps are valid (new version is actually newer)

### Example

In short it turns this:

```
{
	"Path": "github.com/BurntSushi/locker",
	"Version": "v0.0.0-20171006230638-a6e239ea1c69",
	"Time": "2017-10-06T23:06:38Z",
	"GoMod": "/home/mojo/go/pkg/mod/cache/download/github.com/!burnt!sushi/locker/@v/v0.0.0-20171006230638-a6e239ea1c69.mod"
}
{
	"Path": "github.com/BurntSushi/toml",
	"Version": "v0.0.0-20170626110600-a368813c5e64",
	"Time": "2017-06-26T11:06:00Z",
	"Update": {
		"Path": "github.com/BurntSushi/toml",
		"Version": "v0.3.1",
		"Time": "2018-08-15T10:47:33Z"
	},
	"GoMod": "/home/mojo/go/pkg/mod/cache/download/github.com/!burnt!sushi/toml/@v/v0.0.0-20170626110600-a368813c5e64.mod"
}
```

into this:

```
+-------------------------------------------+--------------------------------------+------------------------------------+--------+------------------+
|                  MODULE                   |               VERSION                |            NEW VERSION             | DIRECT | VALID TIMESTAMPS |
+-------------------------------------------+--------------------------------------+------------------------------------+--------+------------------+
| github.com/BurntSushi/locker              | v0.0.0-20171006230638-a6e239ea1c69   |                                    | true   | true             |
| github.com/BurntSushi/toml                | v0.0.0-20170626110600-a368813c5e64   | v0.3.1                             | true   | true             |
+-------------------------------------------+--------------------------------------+------------------------------------+--------+------------------+
```

## Installation

```
go install github.com/psampaz/go-mod-outdated@latest
```

## Usage

In the folder where your go.mod lives run:
 
```
go list -u -m -json all | go-mod-outdated
```

to see all modules in table view.

### Show only modules with updates

```
go list -u -m -json all | go-mod-outdated -update
```

### Show only direct dependencies

```
go list -u -m -json all | go-mod-outdated -direct
```

### Show only direct dependencies with updates

```
go list -u -m -json all | go-mod-outdated -update -direct 
```

### Output as markdown table

To output a markdown compatible table, pass the `-style markdown` option:

```
go list -u -m -json all | go-mod-outdated -style markdown 
```

### Important note for Go 1.14 users

If you are using Go 1.14 with vendoring you need to pass **-mod=mod** or **-mod=readonly** to the go list command otherwise you will get the following error:

```
$ go list -u -m -json all
 
go list -m: can't determine available upgrades using the vendor directory
        (Use -mod=mod or -mod=readonly to bypass.)
```

The following will work:

```
go list -u -m -mod=mod -json all | go-mod-outdated
```

```
go list -u -m -mod=readonly -json all | go-mod-outdated
```

### Docker

In the folder where your go.mod lives run:

```
go list -u -m -json all | docker run --rm -i psampaz/go-mod-outdated
```

To use parameters just append:

```
go list -u -m -json all | docker run --rm -i psampaz/go-mod-outdated -update
```

### CI pipelines

Using the -ci flag will make the command exit with non-zero code, breaking your CI pipelines if outdated dependencies are found.

If you want to make your CI pipeline fail if **any direct or indirect** dependency is outdated use the following:

```
go list -u -m -json all | go-mod-outdated -ci
```

If you want to make your CI pipeline fail **only if a direct** dependency is outdated use the following:

```
go list -u -m -json all | go-mod-outdated -direct -ci
```

### Command-line flags

Use the **-h** or **-help** flag to see all available options:

```
$ go-mod-outdated -help

Usage of go-mod-outdated:
  -direct
        List only direct modules
  -update
        List only modules with updates
  -c
```

# go-mod-outdated

An easy way to find outdated dependencies of your Go projects.

go-mod-outdated provides a table view of the **go list -u -m -json all** command which lists all dependencies of a Go project and their available minor and patch updates. It also provides a way to filter indirect dependencies and dependencies without updates.

## What it does

go-mod-outdated takes JSON output from `go list` and converts it into an easy-to-read table format showing:
- Module name
- Current version
- Available new version (if any)
- Whether it's a direct or indirect dependency
- Whether the timestamps are valid (new version is actually newer)

### Example

In short it turns this:

```
{
	"Path": "github.com/BurntSushi/locker",
	"Version": "v0.0.0-20171006230638-a6e239ea1c69",
	"Time": "2017-10-06T23:06:38Z",
	"GoMod": "/home/mojo/go/pkg/mod/cache/download/github.com/!burnt!sushi/locker/@v/v0.0.0-20171006230638-a6e239ea1c69.mod"
}
{
	"Path": "github.com/BurntSushi/toml",
	"Version": "v0.0.0-20170626110600-a368813c5e64",
	"Time": "2017-06-26T11:06:00Z",
	"Update": {
		"Path": "github.com/BurntSushi/toml",
		"Version": "v0.3.1",
		"Time": "2018-08-15T10:47:33Z"
	},
	"GoMod": "/home/mojo/go/pkg/mod/cache/download/github.com/!burnt!sushi/toml/@v/v0.0.0-20170626110600-a368813c5e64.mod"
}
```

into this:

```
+-------------------------------------------+--------------------------------------+------------------------------------+--------+------------------+
|                  MODULE                   |               VERSION                |            NEW VERSION             | DIRECT | VALID TIMESTAMPS |
+-------------------------------------------+--------------------------------------+------------------------------------+--------+------------------+
| github.com/BurntSushi/locker              | v0.0.0-20171006230638-a6e239ea1c69   |                                    | true   | true             |
| github.com/BurntSushi/toml                | v0.0.0-20170626110600-a368813c5e64   | v0.3.1                             | true   | true             |
+-------------------------------------------+--------------------------------------+------------------------------------+--------+------------------+
```

## Installation

```
go install github.com/psampaz/go-mod-outdated@latest
```

## Usage

In the folder where your go.mod lives run:
 
```
go list -u -m -json all | go-mod-outdated
```

to see all modules in table view.

### Show only modules with updates

```
go list -u -m -json all | go-mod-outdated -update
```

### Show only direct dependencies

```
go list -u -m -json all | go-mod-outdated -direct
```

### Show only direct dependencies with updates

```
go list -u -m -json all | go-mod-outdated -update -direct 
```

### Output as markdown table

To output a markdown compatible table, pass the `-style markdown` option:

```
go list -u -m -json all | go-mod-outdated -style markdown 
```

### Important note for Go 1.14 users

If you are using Go 1.14 with vendoring you need to pass **-mod=mod** or **-mod=readonly** to the go list command otherwise you will get the following error:

```
$ go list -u -m -json all
 
go list -m: can't determine available upgrades using the vendor directory
        (Use -mod=mod or -mod=readonly to bypass.)
```

The following will work:

```
go list -u -m -mod=mod -json all | go-mod-outdated
```

```
go list -u -m -mod=readonly -json all | go-mod-outdated
```

### Docker

In the folder where your go.mod lives run:

```
go list -u -m -json all | docker run --rm -i psampaz/go-mod-outdated
```

To use parameters just append:

```
go list -u -m -json all | docker run --rm -i psampaz/go-mod-outdated -update
```

### CI pipelines

Using the -ci flag will make the command exit with non-zero code, breaking your CI pipelines if outdated dependencies are found.

If you want to make your CI pipeline fail if **any direct or indirect** dependency is outdated use the following:

```
go list -u -m -json all | go-mod-outdated -ci
```

If you want to make your CI pipeline fail **only if a direct** dependency is outdated use the following:

```
go list -u -m -json all | go-mod-outdated -direct -ci
```

### Command-line flags

Use the **-h** or **-help** flag to see all available options:

```
$ go-mod-outdated -help

Usage of go-mod-outdated:
  -direct
        List only direct modules
  -update
        List only modules with updates
  -ci
        Non-zero exit code when at least one outdated dependency was found
  -style string
        Output style, pass 'markdown' for a Markdown table (default "default")
```

### Shortcut aliases

If **go list -u -m -json all | go-mod-outdated -update -direct** seems too difficult to remember, you can create shortcuts using aliases:

```
alias gmo="go list -u -m -json all | go-mod-outdated"

alias gmod="go list -u -m -json all | go-mod-outdated -direct"

alias gmou="go list -u -m -json all | go-mod-outdated -update"

alias gmodu="go list -u -m -json all | go-mod-outdated -direct -update"
```  

## Understanding the output

### VALID TIMESTAMPS column

There are cases where the updated version reported by the go list command is actually older than the current one. go-mod-outdated includes a **VALID TIMESTAMPS** column which indicates when this happens, helping you avoid upgrading to a version that might break your application.

### Important note about upgrading

Upgrading an application is the responsibility of the application maintainer. Semantic versioning provides a way to indicate breaking changes, but everything relies on each module developer applying correct version tags. Unless there is a fully automated way to detect breaking changes in a codebase, a good practice to avoid surprises is to write tests and avoid dependencies on modules that are not well maintained and documented.

def infer(path):

package main

import (
	"flag"
	"os"

	"github.com/psampaz/go-mod-outdated/internal/runner"
)

func main() {
	direct := flag.Bool("direct", false, "List only direct modules")
	update := flag.Bool("update", false, "List only modules with updates")
	ci := flag.Bool("ci", false, "Non-zero exit code when at least one outdated dependency was found")
	style := flag.String("style", "default", "Output style, pass 'markdown' for a Markdown table")
	flag.Parse()
	if *style != "markdown" {
		*style = "default"
	}
	os.Exit(runner.Run(os.Stdin, os.Stdout, *update, *direct, *ci, *style))
}

import (

func main() {
	direct := flag.Bool("direct", false, "List only direct modules")
	update := flag.Bool("update", false, "List only modules with updates")
	ci := flag.Bool("ci", false, "Non-zero exit code when at least one outdated dependency was found")

	flag.Parse()

	os.Exit(runner.Run(os.Stdin, os.Stdout, *update, *direct, *ci, *style))

package mod

import "time"

// Module is a representation of a Go module as reported by go list.
type Module struct {
	Path      string
	Version   string
	Versions  []string
	Replace   *Module
	Time      *time.Time
	Update    *Module
	Main      bool
	Indirect  bool
	Dir       string
	GoMod     string
	GoVersion string
	Error     *ModuleError
}

// ModuleError represents an error reported for a module.
type ModuleError struct {
	Err string
}

// InvalidTimestamp reports whether the timestamp of an available
// update is older than the timestamp of the current version.
func (m *Module) InvalidTimestamp() bool {
	module := m
	if m.Replace != nil {
		module = m.Replace
	}
	if module.Update == nil {
		return false
	}
	if module.Time == nil {
		return false
	}
	return module.Update.Time.Before(*module.Time)
}

// HasUpdate reports whether a newer version is available for the module.
func (m *Module) HasUpdate() bool {
	if m.Replace != nil {
		return m.Replace.Update != nil
	}
	return m.Update != nil
}

// CurrentVersion returns the version that is currently in use.
func (m *Module) CurrentVersion() string {
	if m.Replace != nil {
		return m.Replace.Version
	}
	return m.Version
}

// NewVersion returns the version that is available as an update, if any.
func (m *Module) NewVersion() string {
	if m.Replace != nil {
		if m.Replace.Update != nil {
			return m.Replace.Update.Version
		}
		return ""
	}
	if m.Update != nil {
		return m.Update.Version
	}
	return ""
}

package runner

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"io"
	"log"
	"regexp"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
	"unicode"

	"github.com/psampaz/go-mod-outdated/internal/mod"
)

func Run(input io.Reader, output io.Writer, update bool, direct bool, ci bool, style string) int {
	var modules []mod.Module
	// Decode the stream of modules until EOF is reached.
	// A decoding error aborts the run without any output.
	decoder := json.NewDecoder(input)
	for {
		var module mod.Module
		err := decoder.Decode(&module)
		if err == io.EOF {
			break
		}
		if err != nil {
			log.Println(err)
			return 0
		}
		modules = append(modules, module)
	}
	// The main module is never listed. The remaining filters keep
	// only direct modules and only modules with updates if requested.
	filtered := make([]mod.Module, 0, len(modules))
	for _, module := range modules {
		if module.Main || (update && module.Update == nil) || (direct && module.Indirect) {
			continue
		}
		filtered = append(filtered, module)
	}
	// Render the table even if the CI check will fail afterwards.
	renderTable(output, filtered, style)
	if ci && hasOutdated(filtered) {
		return 1
	}
	return 0
}

// hasOutdated reports whether any of the modules has an update.
// It follows the same notion of an available update as the table
// rendering: for a replaced module the update of the replacement
// counts, otherwise the update of the module itself counts.
// The main module and filtered out modules are not considered,
// because hasOutdated is only called with the filtered modules.
func hasOutdated(modules []mod.Module) bool {
	for i := range modules {
		if modules[i].HasUpdate() {
			return true
		}
	}
	return false
}

// renderTable converts the given modules into table rows and writes
// the resulting table to output. The columns hold the module path,
// the version in use, the available update, whether the module is a
// direct dependency and whether the version timestamps are valid.
func renderTable(output io.Writer, modules []mod.Module, style string) {
	if len(modules) == 0 {
		return
	}
	headers := []string{"Module", "Version", "New Version", "Direct", "Valid Timestamps"}
	for i := range headers {
		headers[i] = strings.ToUpper(headers[i])
	}
	// One row is produced for every module, in the given order.
	rows := make([][]string, 0, len(modules))
	for i := range modules {
		module := &modules[i]
		rows = append(rows, []string{
			module.Path,
			module.CurrentVersion(),
			module.NewVersion(),
			strconv.FormatBool(!module.Indirect),
			strconv.FormatBool(!module.InvalidTimestamp()),
		})
	}
	writeTable(output, headers, rows, style)
}

const maxColumnWidth = 30

var ansiPattern = regexp.MustCompile("\x1b\\[([0-9]{1,3}(;[0-9]{1,3})*)?[mK]")

func writeTable(output io.Writer, headers []string, rows [][]string, style string) {
	// Compute the wrapped representation of every cell.
	cellLines := make([][][]string, len(rows))
	for i, row := range rows {
		cellLines[i] = make([][]string, len(headers))
		for j, cell := range row {
			cellLines[i][j] = wrapCell(cell)
		}
	}
	widths := make([]int, len(headers))
	for i, header := range headers {
		widths[i] = displayWidth(header)
	}
	for _, row := range rows {
		for j, cell := range row {
			candidate := 0
			for _, paragraph := range strings.Split(cell, "\n") {
				if w := displayWidth(paragraph); w > candidate {
					candidate = w
				}
			}
			if candidate > maxColumnWidth {
				candidate = maxColumnWidth
			}
			if candidate > widths[j] {
				widths[j] = candidate
			}
		}
	}
	for _, rowLines := range cellLines {
		for j, lines := range rowLines {
			for _, line := range lines {
				if w := displayWidth(line); w > widths[j] {
					widths[j] = w
				}
			}
		}
	}

	var b strings.Builder
	borderLine := func(left string, fill string, sep string, right string) {
		b.WriteString(left)
		for i, w := range widths {
			if i > 0 {
				b.WriteString(sep)
			}
			b.WriteString(strings.Repeat(fill, w+2))
		}
		b.WriteString(right)
		b.WriteString("\n")
	}
	rowLine := func(cells []string, header bool) {
		b.WriteString("|")
		for j, cell := range cells {
			b.WriteString(padCell(cell, widths[j], header))
			b.WriteString("|")
		}
		b.WriteString("\n")
	}
	headerCells := func() {
		b.WriteString("|")
		for j, header := range headers {
			b.WriteString(padCell(header, widths[j], true))
			b.WriteString("|")
		}
		b.WriteString("\n")
	}
	_ = rowLine

	markdown := style == "markdown"
	if !markdown {
		borderLine("+", "-", "+", "+")
	}

// wrapCell reflows a cell so that none of its lines is wider than the
// longest line in the original cell, capped at maxColumnWidth. The
// lines are chosen so that the squared slack of all but the last line
// is as small as possible.
func wrapCell(cell string) []string {
	paragraphs := strings.Split(cell, "\n")
	limit := 0
	for _, paragraph := range paragraphs {
		if w := displayWidth(paragraph); w > limit {

		}

	}

	words := strings.Split(joined, " ")

// one minimising the sum of squared slack over all but the last line
// is used; ties keep the earliest possible line break.
func wrapWords(words []string, limit int) []string {

	}

	for i, word := range words {
